title: Supported information flows satisfy declared trust and confidentiality constraints
statement: Every supported explicit information flow MUST satisfy project-defined Function Contract source, sink, endorsement, and declassification semantics, while unknown and unsupported flow MUST remain explicit non-evidence.
rationale: Nominal, value-domain, typestate, and effect correctness do not prevent insufficiently trusted or overly confidential information from reaching a consumer that forbids it.
failure_prevented: Supported information carrying a prohibited integrity or confidentiality classification reaching a declared consumer boundary, or a security classification changing without explicit trusted-transition authority.
applicability: Legacy finite facets and distributed Function Contracts retain their meaning. Operation Policy v2 declarations apply only to sinks in an explicitly selected GOV-FORTRESS-DECLARED-FLOW project or Module scope, bound to an exact PSM context. Unknown aliases, dispatch, implicit flows, concurrency and incomplete evidence remain explicit.
evaluation: Reuse finite facet propagation over supported PSM movements. Check operation and Function Contract bounds independently, preserve raw findings and provenance, disclose every transformation assumption and claim-relative coverage limitation. An assumed sanitizer is not implementation proof.

finding.message: A supported information flow violates its consumer's declared integrity or confidentiality constraint.

remediation: Preserve the incoming classification, satisfy the consumer boundary, or declare and review a truthful explicit endorsement or declassification where that trust boundary is intended.
valid_example: A value classified VALIDATED reaches a parameter requiring integrity at least VALIDATED, or an explicit reviewed endorsement transforms UNTRUSTED input to VALIDATED output.
invalid_example: UNTRUSTED input reaches a sink requiring VALIDATED data, or SECRET data reaches a sink permitting at most INTERNAL data without explicit declassification.
exception_policy: Unknown and unsupported flow never becomes proof. No naming convention, sanitizer heuristic, or transitive call merely authorizes an integrity increase or confidentiality decrease.
history: Introduced with project-defined ordered facets, Function Contract v3 flow declarations, conservative explicit propagation, and trusted-transition diagnostics.
Added explicitly selected, exact-context operation declarations and claim-relative evidence without changing legacy Function Contract conclusions.
